title: The caves, with the rock taken away
question: The honeycomb web and the round room are two different things sharing one cave. Should the web stay at all — as background rock you dig through, never as passage — or go entirely, leaving caves as passages and rooms only?
context_md:
One cave system in a full-size world (terraced, seed 1), photographed from inside. Left is what you would see; right is the same frame with every open cell painted magenta, so the cave's own shape is visible through the rock.

What the second picture shows is that the cave **is** the honeycomb — the passages are the straight boundary lines of a Voronoi diagram, meeting three at a time — with a single circle grown on top of it as the one room. That circle is the 'perfect oval' you named. Nothing else in the picture is a room.

Measured today, same build: the web's corridors are too narrow for the gnome over more than half their length, so most of what looks like cave is not walkable. I am redesigning this from scratch and the answer to the question above decides whether the web is kept as scenery or removed.
